items.title: Olive Bar & Kitchen
items.why: A whitewashed Mediterranean restaurant in a courtyard facing the Qutub Minar. Book for dinner and ask for a table under the trees.
items.coordsFrom: approximate (One Style Mile, Kalka Das Marg)

items.title: Qla
items.why: A terrace restaurant with a view of the Qutub Minar. Come at sunset for a drink, then stay for dinner.

items.title: Cafe Dori
items.why: An Italian café in the Dhan Mill compound for pasta, pizza and a long lunch.

items.title: Potbelly
items.why: A rooftop in Shahpur Jat serving Bihari food. Order litti chokha and the mutton curry.

items.title: Kampai
items.why: A Japanese restaurant in Aerocity's Worldmark for ramen and sushi, with a tatami room.

items.title: Comorin
items.area: Two Horizon Centre, Golf Course Road
items.why: A modern Indian restaurant and bar on Golf Course Road for inventive small plates and cocktails.

items.title: House of Celeste
items.why: A restaurant in the 32nd Avenue courtyard for Indian food and cocktails.

items.title: Khan Market
items.why: Delhi's smartest small market, two rows of shops with cafés upstairs. Start at Bahrisons and Full Circle for books, walk the boutiques, then climb to a café for lunch.

items.title: Janpath and the Tibetan Market
items.why: A long pavement of stalls selling silver jewellery, scarves, embroidered bags and handicrafts, with the Tibetan Market's covered row at its heart. Look at a few stalls before you buy, and bargain with a smile.

items.title: Sarojini Nagar Market
items.why: Delhi's bargain market, full of export-surplus clothes at street prices. Go on a weekday morning before the crowds, check seams carefully, and start at half the asking price.

items.title: Chandni Chowk bazaars
items.area: Kinari Bazaar, Dariba Kalan and Katra Neel, Chandni Chowk
items.why: The old city's wedding bazaars: Kinari Bazaar for trims and tinsel, Dariba Kalan for silver, and the katras off the main street for fabric by the metre. Take the metro, go in the morning, and stop for parathas between lanes.
items.coordsFrom: approximate (Kinari Bazaar, Dariba Kalan and Katra Neel, Chandni Chowk)

items.title: Dilli Haat, INA
items.why: An open-air crafts market where artisans from every state sell handlooms, pottery and metalwork in rotating stalls, with a food court of regional kitchens. Shop in the afternoon, then eat momos from the Northeast stalls.

items.title: GK I M-Block and N-Block markets
items.why: Two neighbouring South Delhi markets of fashion labels and Indian-wear stores, with cafés and bars upstairs. Shop in the afternoon, then stay on for dinner.

items.title: GK II M-Block Market
items.why: A smaller, calmer market ringed with restaurants and cafés. Come in the evening for a walk round the block and dinner.

items.title: Shahpur Jat designer lanes
items.why: An urban village whose narrow lanes are full of independent designers' studios for bridal and occasion wear. Wander slowly, look up at the upper floors, and stop for coffee or ramen between shops.

items.title: Meherchand Market
items.why: A quiet row of concept stores, homeware, and small labels by the Lodhi Colony murals. Pair it with the Lodhi Art District walk and a coffee.

items.title: South Extension I and II
items.why: Long-established fashion and occasion-wear stores on both sides of Ring Road, from saree houses to big labels. Go with a list; it is where Delhi buys for weddings.

items.title: Kamla Nagar Market
items.why: The student market beside Delhi University's North Campus: cheap clothes, shoes and accessories, with momos, chole bhature and cafés in the lanes. Busiest in the late afternoon.

items.title: Karol Bagh and Ajmal Khan Road
items.why: A loud, packed shopping street for clothing, wedding outfits and jewellery, with Gaffar Market's electronics nearby. Go on a weekday afternoon; it closes on Mondays.

items.title: Galleria Market
items.why: Gurugram's neighbourhood market, a ring of everyday shops, bakeries and cafés around a courtyard. Come for coffee and an easy errand run.

items.title: Sector 18 and Atta Market
items.why: Noida's central shopping district, where Atta Market's budget stalls sit beside the showrooms of Sector 18 and near the big malls. Good for everyday finds and dinner after.

items.title: INJA
items.why: Fine dining that joins Indian and Japanese cooking in a quiet boutique hotel. Take the tasting menu and book ahead.

items.title: Bukhara
items.why: The famous tandoor restaurant at ITC Maurya, where you eat with your hands at low wooden tables. Order the dal Bukhara, sikandari raan and a giant naan for the table.

items.title: Dum Pukht
items.why: Awadhi cooking at ITC Maurya, slow-cooked in sealed pots. Order the dum pukht biryani and the galouti kebab.

items.title: Baoshuan
